title: Chapter 10 — Refrigeration
intro: The highest-traffic category — configurations, capacity logic, feature tiers, and the five questions every refrigerator sale starts with.

sections.title: The Category That Drives Traffic
sections.content:
Refrigeration is the most-shopped appliance category. It is often the anchor of a kitchen package and the product customers research most before visiting a store.

Knowing refrigeration deeply is non-negotiable. If you cannot speak confidently about configurations, capacity, features, and installation requirements, you will lose the category that generates the most floor traffic.

sections.title: Configurations
sections.content:
Top freezer — entry level, reliable, best value per cubic foot. Bottom freezer — puts fresh food at eye level, ergonomic advantage. Side-by-side — equal access to both sections, narrow door swing for tight spaces. French door — the most popular premium configuration, wide shelves, bottom freezer drawer. Column — separate full-size units, luxury market, maximum flexibility.

Each configuration solves a different problem. Discovery tells you which one fits. Never assume every customer wants a French door just because it is popular.

sections.title: The Five Questions
sections.content:
Every refrigerator sale starts with five questions:

What size opening do you have? Counter depth or standard depth? What finish — stainless, black stainless, white, panel-ready? Do you need an ice maker or water dispenser? What is your budget range?

These five answers narrow 200 refrigerators to 10. That is the power of structured discovery applied to a specific category.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating refrigeration knowledge, ask:

Can the salesperson explain every configuration and who it fits?
Do they ask the five qualifying questions before showing product?
Can they articulate the FAB chain for top features in each tier?
Do they match the product to the customer's kitchen — not just their preference?
